results.question: Why did only my first matching workflow run?
results.expected_answer: Rule processing stops after the first matching rule unless Continue to next rule is enabled.
results.answer:
I'll look up FlowDesk docs about matching workflows and triggers to find likely causes.I don’t have your workspace logs, but here are the most common FlowDesk reasons why only the first matching workflow executed — and what to check/fix. I’ll assume you’re using FlowDesk “matching” rules that route items to workflows when they match criteria.

Possible causes and what to inspect

1) Workflow “stop after match” or exclusive routing behavior
- Many matching systems stop at the first successful match unless you enable “run all matching workflows” or “continue evaluating rules.” Check the workflow or routing rule settings for an option like “stop on match,” “first match wins,” or “exclusive” and turn it off if you want multiple workflows to run.

2) Trigger type is “one-shot” or “single-run”
- Some triggers are designed to fire only once per item (for example, when an item transitions state). If the trigger fired and marked the item as handled, later workflows won’t re-trigger. Look for per-item trigger limits or flags such as “only run once per record.”

3) Workflow conditions changed after the first run
- The first workflow may have modified the item (fields, state, tags, owner), so the item no longer meets the other workflows’ conditions. Check what changes the first workflow makes and whether those changes remove the item from other workflows’ criteria.

4) Workflow ordering and priority
- Workflows may be evaluated in a specified order; lower-priority workflows might not run if higher-priority one handles the item. Confirm the evaluation order or priority settings and adjust if you want multiple to run.

5) Concurrency, locking, or deduplication logic
- Some systems lock a record while a workflow runs, preventing simultaneous workflows. Or there may be deduplication logic that prevents duplicate workflow executions. Check for locks, in-progress flags, or dedupe settings.

6) Failed/paused workflows or exhausted retry limits
- If subsequent workflows attempted to run but failed, they might be paused or throttled. Look at the execution history/queue for errors or retry limits.

7) Permissions or activation state
- Ensure the other workflows are active and the account/workflow has permission to act on the item type. An inactive workflow won’t run.

8) Time-based or delayed conditions
- If other workflows expect different timing (e.g., scheduled/delayed triggers), they might not run immediately after the first workflow.

How to troubleshoot quickly

- Check the matching/routing settings for “stop on first match” or similar.
- Inspect the run history/log for the item: which workflows ran, which were skipped, and any error messages.
- Reproduce with a test item and add logging or temporary no-op steps to see evaluation order and condition changes.
- Compare the item state before and after the first workflow to see which condition was invalidated.
- If available, toggle a setting to “evaluate all matching workflows” and test again.
